Players control a team of gem-hungry goblins racing uncontrollable mine carts underground to retrieve the most jewels before the earth collapses into the deadly chasm below! Easy to pick up and play but with a compelling strategic puzzle for more hardened gamers to master, Off the Rails combines thoughtful tile placement and planning with cut-throat racing and out of control anticipation! Culminating in the total destruction of the board, can you leave your opponents eating your gold-dust and escape the chasm with the most expensive gems? To do this, players must lay connected routes of Track Tiles in order to run their clan’s minecarts from the Surface to the shiny Jewels and back again. The player with the highest value of Jewels retrieved wins! Setup Mines There are 4 Mines in the middle of the board. Each Mine features a centre square surrounded by 8 Mine squares numbered 1 to 8. Each Mine has a different colour and Clan icon: Red Yellow Green Blue Jewels Jewels are drawn randomly from the supply throughout the game Jewel # Ruby 24 Emerald 15 Gold 10 Diamond 5 Decks and Initial Jewel Placement There are 8 Red, 8 Yellow, 8 Green, and 8 Blue Deposit Cards, each numbered 1 through 8, which are shuffled separately before the game begins. 1 card of each colour is removed from the game. If playing with 2 or 3 players, an additional card of each colour is removed. 1 card of each colour is revealed and jewel deposits are made at the corresponding Mine location. 1 card of each colour is placed in the Chasm Deck area. A Chasm Token from each colour Mine is placed on top of the Chasm Deck. The remaining cards are placed in piles of 4, 1 from each colour, shuffled independently and stacked to create the Deposit Deck. The Chasm Deposit Card is shuffled between the 5th and 8th bottom card in the Deposit Deck. Chasm Tokens There are 5 Red, 5 Yellow, 5 Green, and 5 Blue Chasm Tokens in total. One Chasm Token of each colour is placed on the Chasm Deck during setup, the remaining tokens are mixed and placed into a supply to be drawn randomly later. Player Order The first player chooses which side of the board to begin on The second player begins on the opposite side from the first player. The third player takes one of the remaining sides randomly, with the fourth player opposite them. Then each player takes the 2 corresponding mine carts of their colour, placing one white and one black speed die in each, with the '3' face showing. [Rating: 2/10] 2021-06-01 : First play. Typical KickStarter game where after coming up with the initial cool sounding idea, making a decent game of it was only an afterthought. I don't mind randomness if a game allows you to play the odds, to push your luck, but this is pure chaos.

[Rating: 3/10] This is a game about piling gems into mine carts and crashing mine carts. Neither are really my cup of tea.

[Rating: 3/10] *3* (Initial Plays) Super chaotic game of gathering gems with carts, in which I did not care for at all. There were too many random elements happening for this to be fun for me. I will likely never play this again.

[Rating: 4/10] FIRST IMPRESSION:  There's some fun in the box but I'd rather just play Pompei which reminds me of this game. There's the buildup where everyone is going around setting up and gathering points and then the teardown/destruction where it is get out while you can. However, in this game, there is the risk of collision and derailment which can hurt you considerably as all gems are removed if you were derailed. In some cases, you just lose a couple gems. Probably best two player as there would be a great deal of chaos in a 3+ player game with mine carts everywhere.

[Rating: 4/10] Too long, and a bit too convoluted, for the amount of fun and interest I was getting from it.

[Rating: 4/10] Had a pretty frustrating first play of this. About 2/3 into the game both carts lost to the chasm...so you get to sit and pass the rest of your turns. eh  Had this been a shorter game (tsuro comes to mind), no big deal. I actually kind of liked it until that point...the player elimination in a game longer than 15 minutes is kind of rough.

[Rating: 4/10] An interesting idea, building tracks with the intent to collide into other players sounds like fun. The randomness of where the player eliminating chasms open up, spoil the endgame though.
